blocks.text: By accessing the AI Access Graph service, you provide Zscaler the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs. For AI Access Graph, logs include:

blocks.item: Cloud Service Provider (CSP) activity audit logs

blocks.text: In addition, subject to your configuration and enablement, the following logs are also processed:

blocks.item: Data residing in cloud data stores such as databases, storage services, and data volumes (disks) is scanned and classified. Raw data is not saved, only metadata is stored and reported.
Data systems are scanned for security vulnerabilities, and information about any discovered security vulnerabilities is stored.

blocks.text: All logs that describe active cloud resources or issues are retained by Zscaler for the duration of the subscription. Once the resources are no longer present in the CSP, AI Access Graph maintains the logs for a rolling period of 180 days during the term of the subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, Zscaler deletes the logs after the 180-day retention cycle or earlier upon request.
AI Access Graph logs are stored in the United States.
